title: Trumpet night at the Bandbox and Chick Webb takes him in
summary: Told to try the Bandbox jam sessions, he played trumpet night, and Chick Webb came, paid his landlady and took him in.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That was our dinner. So we don't know -- so we run into some people and they say, "So what are you guys doing?" A musician, I think, one of the guys was. "They ain't doing nothing, man." "We need a job." Said, "Why don't you all go over to New York?" We said, "We're in New York."
(Laughter)

So they said, "No, go over to Manhattan. They have jam sessions over at the Bandbox, for different nights. They have trumpet night, saxophone night, piano players' night, trombone night." So we goes over there and we find out what night. So I go in there and -- trumpet night.
Where was the Bandbox?
The Bandbox was at 131st, I think, between Lenox and Seventh, near Seventh Avenue.
Yeah.

Yeah. So I go in there one night, with my trumpet, on trumpet night, and I started blowing. Somebody go get Chick Webb. Somebody went and got Chick Webb. And he listened to me play. "Where you come from, boy?"
(Laughter)
And I told him the story, after I got through blowing.
Did you know who you were talking to?

No. I didn't know who I was talking to. So he says, "Well, come on. I'll go over there to get your things." I said, "I owe the landlady money. I have to pay the landlady before I can get out." So he went over and he paid the landlady up and I moved in with him.
No kidding.
Yeah.

-- and we're going to go back and see -- I wonder why there's a line on that thing somewhere. Yes, I hear something making a noise. I wonder if that thing -- no. Okay, Cootie, you say you told Chick you owed the landlady.
Yeah. So Chick said, 'Well, that's okay. Come on#.' He took me over in a taxicab.
Took you over in a taxicab. Well, how come he had so much cash on hand?
I don't know. He wasn't working. And we went over there and picked up my bags, paid the landlady.
What about Edmond Hall? He wasn't with you?
No.
You'd gone alone.
Yeah. Because it was trumpet night.
Yeah.
And they didn't allow saxophone players in there.
Yeah.
On trumpet night.
Yeah.
I don't know if Edmond Hall was with me or not. He could have been with me.
Yeah. But anyway, you --
So we went on back over there.
